## Revision 9 depth numerator — 2026-10-19

Plan [revision 3](full-live-specification-plan.md#revision-3--depth-before-breadth-2026-10-19)
orders depth before new breadth by user direction. The only numerator that may
be reported against the frozen denominator is: per owner, required outcomes
graded by X/S/shipped data, required outcomes still U with a named closure
route, and required outcomes with no route under ADR 0003; per inventory,
complete device profiles and reviewed family contracts. Catalog rows, case
counts and page counts remain excluded. No denominator, closure gate, evidence
rule, seal rule or execution authorization changes.

## Revision 10 candidate conformance numerator — 2026-10-19

Plan [revision 3](full-live-specification-plan.md#revision-3--depth-before-breadth-2026-10-19)
was amended the same day to a vertical-slice rule: the T1 candidate, built in
the provisioned implementation worktree, pulls analyst depth through
implementation questions and failed released cases; two capability gates and
the ungraded released cases are the only analyst-initiated depth. The
reportable numerator gains one term: per family, released cases the candidate
passes over released cases, with the release path pinned and the comparison
rule stated; that is the Candidate conformance state above. Documentary breadth
stops opening new owners. No denominator, closure gate, evidence rule, seal rule
or execution authorization changes; the candidate remains forbidden in the
analyst checkout.

### Selection rule

1. Candidate-raised items: an `IQ-` entry in `wiki/implementation/questions.md`
   on branch `impl` (read with `git show impl:wiki/implementation/questions.md`
   or after merging `impl` into `main`), or a released case the candidate fails
   for a specification reason. Answer through a successor revision and release
   of the owning family. These are depth packets by construction.
2. Capability gates, one X provider at a time: D-01 Corpus complete profile and
   D-03 Utility in-binary feasibility (table below). They answer whether device
   DSP beyond the five released bundles can be specified at all.
3. D-02: ungraded or unknown cases in the 19 current releases, and T1 unknowns
   the candidate hits; not a sweep of every U mark.
4. Independent review of a frozen successor from 1–3, and release of the revised
   family (T1.5 continues).
5. Breadth only when nothing above is ready for the agent's evidence route.
   Breadth packets in flight at adoption finish normally: the Synthesis owner R3
   review, the Legacy and Distortion owner successors, and the Automation
   192-block and Project §5.4–5.10 source audits. No new full-chapter source
   audit, typed-API family, controller profile or owner opens.

Exit evidence for 1–3 reports the owner's
[depth numerator](full-live-specification-design.md#revision-9-depth-numerator--2026-10-19)
counts; candidate conformance is reported per family as released cases passing
over released cases ([design revision 10](full-live-specification-design.md#revision-10-candidate-conformance-numerator--2026-10-19)).
Root copies both into the owner's F-row, the feature map and verification
coverage. No fraction is reported without them.

Next D01 depth preparation: after its R6 owner freeze, Synthesis proposes a
compact required-outcome ledger from existing Corpus clauses, selected linked
Corpus workflow/position obligations and retained preflight gaps. This is a
private denominator/closure-route proposal, not an independently frozen
denominator or new graded outcomes. Preserve unresolved behavioral continua
and cross-owner obligations instead of treating parameter vectors, case counts
or source hops as complete coverage. No new source audit, original call or
candidate work is selected by this preparation.
